summary: Memory-bound case: amdclang's build is at headroom 1.15-1.17 over the memory floor (537 MB read + 537 MB written, each element touched once), so 1.5x is out of reach in principle. The shipped state 62cd89da2d507f40 is a source rewrite with 2 elements per thread (global_load_dwordx2 / store_dwordx2, v_pk_mul), block 128, grid cdiv(N, 256), with a scalar tail loop for the last partial group and the original null-pointer checks kept; arithmetic is unchanged (bit-identical per element). It measured 1.143x (240 pairs, CI 1.1405-1.1448; 60 pairs 1.139), 0.1916 ms, headroom 1.01, i.e. at the floor.

tried.speedup: 1.111 (60 pairs), 1.103 (240 pairs); about +1% over its parent, within run-to-run spread

tried.outcome: not attempted: the listing of c08d83a20d307330 already issues both loads before any wait and is straight-line; at headroom 1.01-1.04 no measurable gain was expected

friction: Run-to-run spread of the same state against ref is 1-2% (e5dd538d8bf5c8c5: 1.108 at 60 pairs, 1.089 at 240), comparable to the differences between block-size variants; ranking needed compare(a, b, 240) each time. A tool that ranks N verified states in one interleaved run would replace several benches.

source sweeps with like= return the full state record for each variant and each needs a separate check and bench call; a single sweep call (defines grid -> check + bench table) would have cut the session roughly in half.
No way to express non-temporal / streaming stores or any cache hint, which is the only remaining idea for a kernel at the floor that writes as many bytes as it reads.

The first bench of ref in this session reported reference_headroom 1.29 (reference 0.244 ms, clock-level drift) against 1.15-1.17 later: the headroom figure moves with the clock level, so one reading is not enough to decide whether 1.5x is possible.
lessons: mo_prelu_bwd (2 input streams, 2 output streams, 4 bytes per lane each, N = 2^26): amdclang is at headroom 1.15-1.17; several elements per thread recovers it to headroom 1.01 (1.14x). This is a memory-floor kernel: 1.5x is not available.

Elements per thread x block size at fixed bytes: 2 per thread block 128 = 1.143 (1 KB contiguous per stream per workgroup, 512 B per wave); 2/64 = 1.09-1.11; 2/256 = 1.097; 4/64 = 1.103; 4/256 = 1.098; 4/128 = 1.076; 4/1024 = 1.052; 8/256 = 1.044. 8 bytes per lane with two waves per workgroup was best, 5% ahead of the next (direct compare 1.049); 32 bytes per lane and block 1024 are clearly worse.

coarsen on the one-element-per-thread ref of a 4-stream kernel loses (0.87 / 0.83 / 0.76), unlike axpy/gelu; coarsen factor 2 on a 2-per-thread block-64 state is about +1% (not distinguishable from noise). Restructure at the source level instead.

amdclang compiles an ext_vector_type(N) load plus a per-element select loop into global_load_dwordxN, v_pk_mul_f32 and per-element v_cmp/v_cndmask with no spills; a scalar tail loop for the partial last group costs nothing on the full path and passes all battery shapes.

session.final:
The session is finished and the report is recorded: the best verified state is `62cd89da2d507f40` at **1.143x** over amdclang (240 pairs, CI 1.1405–1.1448; 0.1916 ms against 0.2193 ms). The 1.5x target was not reached and is out of reach in principle for this kernel.

- **Why 1.5x is not available:** this is the memory-bound case. amdclang's build already sits at headroom 1.15–1.17 over the memory floor, with every element touched once (537 MB read, 537 MB written). The shipped state is at headroom 1.01.
- **What the winning state does:** a source rewrite with 2 elements per thread, block 128 and grid `cdiv(N, 256)`, with a scalar tail loop for the last partial group. The arithmetic and the null-pointer checks are unchanged. It passes the static check and the full battery (49/49).
- **Other variants:** nine other source variants (2, 4 or 8 elements per thread, blocks 64 to 1024) and one `coarsen` on top were all wins, between 1.04x and 1.11x. A direct 240-pair compare puts the shipped state 1.049x ahead of the next best.
- **Not attempted:** machine-IR edits on the source states. The listing already issues both loads before any wait, so I expected nothing measurable this close to the floor.

The harness will re-verify with its own two 240-pair timings. Same-state timings drifted by 1–2% between runs here, so expect its figure to land near, not exactly on, 1.14x.
